subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education, KS3-KS4 core PE); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, resilience, leadership, lifelong activity) adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Heart rate zones and perceived effort
objectives: Estimate maximum heart rate and training zones
Use the 1 to 10 effort scale to control intensity

keywords.def: the highest heart rate you can reach, estimated as 220 minus your age
about 50 to 70 percent of maximum heart rate
about 70 to 85 percent of maximum heart rate
rating of perceived exertion: how hard exercise feels

starter: Bismillah. What does FITT stand for?
How do you take your pulse at the wrist?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Warm up for at least 5 minutes
Do not push to maximum effort
Stop if you feel dizzy, faint or have chest pain
Never exercise when unwell; tell an adult
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Estimating maximum heart rate
teach.note: Emphasise it is a rough guide only and people vary. Do not push pupils to reach a maximum; safety first.

teach.heading: Training zones
bullets: For a 14-year-old: about 124 to 175 bpm in the combined zone
teach.note: Check the calculation: 206 x 0.6 = 124, 206 x 0.85 = 175. Misconception: higher zone is always better; different zones train different things.

teach.heading: Taking the pulse
bullets: Take it at rest and after 3 minutes of jogging
teach.note: Pupils record resting and working pulse privately. Do not compare with others.

teach.heading: Effort scale
teach.note: Pupils match their pulse numbers to how hard it felt. Link to listening to your body.

independent: Calculate your estimated maximum heart rate and zones.
Take a resting pulse and record it.
exit: Complete 3 minutes of jogging and record pulse and effort.
Write whether you were in the moderate or vigorous zone and why.
homework: Why is the 220 minus age formula only an estimate?
lessons.send: Take your resting pulse each morning for three days and find the average.

lessons.title: Design a personal exercise programme
objectives: Apply FITT and progression to a four-week plan
Evaluate the safety and balance of your plan

keywords.def: including a range of activity types in a plan
to judge how well something worked

starter: What zone is 60 percent of maximum heart rate?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Talk to a parent before starting new plans
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: SMART goals
teach.note: Give a poor goal ('get fitter') and a SMART goal and ask pupils to compare.

teach.heading: Plan structure
bullets: Add a rest day after hard days
teach.note: Show a model weekly table. Misconception: more sessions are always better.

teach.heading: Progression
teach.note: Progress by small steps. Add a deload (easier) week if feeling tired.

teach.heading: Write and evaluate
teach.note: Pairs use criteria: SMART, FITT, balance, rest.

practice: What does the S in SMART stand for?
independent: Write a SMART goal for one component of fitness.
Fill the first week of a plan table.
exit: Complete a four-week plan with FITT and progression.
Evaluate it against the safety checklist.
homework: Rewrite 'get stronger' as a SMART goal.
lessons.send: Start week one of your plan and note how it felt.
